## PLAN ROUND 1 · publish · task first-edition

**Facts found**
- There are five runbooks: cert-expiry, deploy-rollback, disk-full, dns-failure and queue-backlog
  (`runbooks/`).
- Three of them name an internal host or a secret path, each on line 3:
  - `runbooks/disk-full.md:3` names `db-primary-01.int.example.net`.
  - `runbooks/queue-backlog.md:3` names `jobs-01.int.example.net`.
  - `runbooks/cert-expiry.md:3` names `secret/platform/acme-token`.

  deploy-rollback and dns-failure name neither.
- `scripts/check.sh` checks two things: every runbook's first line starts with "Use when", and
  every `](./…)` link resolves. It knows nothing about hosts or secrets.
- `STANDARDS.md` has one rule: a runbook's first line says when to use it. It says nothing about
  redaction or publishing.
- The repo has no git remote and no CI (`.git/config`). There's no `mkdocs.yml` and no pandoc
  config.
- `.claude/marathon.toml` has no `[remote] publish`, so SHIP merges the task branch locally.
- Every format sits behind single sign-on, and one access group covers all three. So the audience
  is that group whatever the format, and the redaction pass depends only on the audience
  (`context/publishing.md`).
- Whether MkDocs or pandoc is installed locally is unchecked.

**Currency**
- cwd: no currency command

**Questions**

1. **Format of the first edition: MkDocs static site, single PDF, or a Markdown index in the
   repo?**
   - **rec:** MkDocs static site. During an incident it's searchable and linkable. MkDocs is the
     standard tool for this, so nothing gets custom-built. Its cost: with no remote and no CI, the
     first build and the upload to the internal docs host are done by hand. A Markdown index
     needs no build, but the repo has no remote to browse. A PDF works offline, but old copies
     outlive every edit.
   - **changes:** adds an MkDocs config over the existing runbooks and a build step. Round 2 then
     asks how the site reaches the docs host and whether a strict MkDocs build joins the check.
2. **Audience of the first edition: on-call engineers only, or on-call engineers plus the support
   team?**
   - **rec:** on-call plus support. Support asked for read access in the last quarterly review.
     The redaction is three lines: two internal hostnames, in disk-full and queue-backlog, and one
     secret path, in cert-expiry. Its cost: on-call engineers lose those three names from the text
     unless something points to them.
   - **changes:** adds a redaction slice for those three runbooks and a rule that keeps new
     runbooks free of hosts and secret paths. Round 2 asks what replaces the redacted names and
     whether the check enforces the rule or `STANDARDS.md` states it. Answering "on-call only"
     drops both.

**reply:** "1 ok, 2 ok", or "1 PDF, 2 …"

Round 2 depends on these answers. It covers how the edition reaches the docs host or file share,
what replaces the redacted names, and whether to add a remote and CI now. The brief will probably
be a one-way door: once readers outside the repo have the edition, it can't be pulled back.
